# Conscription and the mass army (`conscription_mass_army`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/military.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Warfare, security & deterrence (`military`)
- Deps: helped by census_vital_registration, standing_army_logistics, railway, universal_schooling
- Core idea: Every fit man owes military service for a fixed term, is trained in peacetime and then passes to a reserve that can be called up. This gives armies of hundreds of thousands at low cost and ties the population to the state. It needs a register of who exists, a way to feed, arm and officer the numbers, and a population that accepts the duty, which usually means that service brings rights, land or citizenship. The reserve system matters most: a short-service army with trained reserves outnumbers a long-service professional army several times on mobilisation.
- Pitfalls:
  - Raising numbers that cannot be fed, armed or led; untrained masses are slaughtered
  - Substitutes and exemptions for the rich destroy acceptance
  - Conscripts desert in thousands when forced to serve far from home without pay
  - Believing the French levy of 1793 was the first; Qin and Han China and republican Rome ran universal levies two thousand years earlier
- History: china: 4th–3rd c. BC – universal male service in Qin after Shang Yang's reforms, continued under the Western Han; rome: by 3rd c. BC – annual levy (dilectus) of propertied citizens described by Polybius; by 50 BC legally in force but largely replaced by volunteers; americas: 15th c. – Inca rotational labour service (mit'a) includes army duty; islamic: 1820s – Muhammad Ali conscripts Egyptian peasants; europe: 1620s – Swedish allotment levy; 1733 – Prussian canton system; 1793 – French levée en masse; 1798 – Jourdan law; 1814 – Prussian universal service with reserves; east_asia: 1873 – Japanese conscription law
- Read:
  - Polybius, Histories VI.19–26
  - William H. McNeill, The Pursuit of Power (1982)
  - Alan Forrest, Conscripts and Deserters: The Army and French Society during the Revolution and Empire (1989)
